title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 3 vs. San Francisco 49ers
headline: Jeremiyah Love's workload rose and the coach said he handled it well, but his role going forward is week-to-week; the run game was efficient with no explosive plays (longest rush 8 yards).
summary: LaFleur said there were no injuries of note after the Week 3 loss to San Francisco; anyone who got banged up returned to the game. He explained the late field goal as a way to get to a one-score game and keep a normal offense on the field if an onside kick was recovered. He blamed penalties for stalling drives, especially early, and said the offense was efficient but not explosive: the run game was hitting, but the longest rush was only eight yards, and he expects one to pop eventually. He said the offensive line did some good things, but pass protection got leaky on Jacoby (Brissett) when they took shots off play action, so he will review what they ask of the line on those plays. The defense needs to clean up its rush lanes, tackling and pressure on a mobile quarterback. He said the blitz-heavy plans were specific to the first three weeks and that week four will differ. He said Jeremiyah Love got into a groove with a bigger workload and handled it well, but would not commit to continued increased usage and said it will be decided week to week. He also explained the heavy base-defense usage as a response to three opponents with fullbacks and multiple tight ends, praised Jack Gibbens and said the team trusts Cody Simon.

signals.claim: Love's workload was increased in this game, but his future role will be decided week to week.
signals.note: Love got a bigger share and performed well, but the coach declined to promise he keeps it, so the volume is not locked in.

signals.claim: Pass protection on play-action shot plays was leaky, and the staff will review how long they ask the line to hold up.
signals.note: Pressure on deeper play-action shots could limit the downfield passing game until protection or play design is adjusted.
signals.quote: it got, uh, you know, a little bit leaky on Jacoby.

signals.claim: Simon is trusted as one of the base-defense linebackers on the field.
signals.note: Base-heavy usage keeps him on the field, which supports IDP value.
signals.quote: We have a lot of trust in Cody Simon too.

signals.claim: Gibbens is playing well as a base-defense linebacker and keeps his role.
signals.note: Base-heavy alignments keep him on the field, which supports IDP value.
signals.quote: Gibby's done a really good job.

topics.detail: The run game was efficient and often put the team in second-and-manageable, but there were no explosive runs (longest was 8 yards). LaFleur expects one to pop eventually.
Penalties repeatedly knocked the offense back and were called the story of the game. The offense scored when it played clean in the second half.
The team needs better pass rush, disciplined rush lanes and tackling against a quarterback who escapes well. The coach gave no detailed evaluation, saying he needs to see the tape.
The team has played a lot of base defense because the first three opponents used fullbacks and multiple tight ends. LaFleur said next week will look different against a different scheme.
The team kicked a field goal inside the 35 to make it a one-score game, so a recovered onside kick would let them run normal plays rather than only a Hail Mary.

title: Joe Brady Talks What He Learned From the 24-16 Victory Over the Chargers
headline: Bills won 24-16 despite five turnovers; James Cook stays the lead back after two fumbles, Ty Johnson made a big impact in his return, and Christian Benford's injury status is unknown.
summary: Joe Brady took responsibility for five turnovers, calling the offense's ball security "unacceptable" and saying he must call a better game and coach the details. He praised the defense for keeping Buffalo in the game early, singling out C.J. Gardner-Johnson's interception, which he called a huge play, and said he was pleased to see him back on the field after a week of practice. He said the team showed character by not pointing fingers and winning anyway. After Christian Benford went down, Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun got extra snaps. Brady praised Igbinosun's confidence and a sideline tackle, and said Hairston will want a first-drive play back. He said he had no health update on Benford and would evaluate after the game. On Dalton Kincaid's fumble and James Cook's two straight games with a ball punched out, Brady said he wants them fighting for yards but with better ball security, and he told Cook he would still give him the ball on the next play. Cook ran well, especially in the fourth quarter. Ty Johnson drew praise for a designed fourth-down play and a big third-down conversion, with Brady noting he is getting his legs back. Frank Gore Jr. was credited with an outstanding first two weeks. Brady said Greg Rousseau is playing a slightly different position, now in a two-point stance with eyes in the backfield, and is confident. That should open up opportunities for Ed Oliver, Dion Dawkins and Bradley Chubb. Brady also said he must review the pass-protection breakdowns that put hits on Josh Allen, starting with his own play calling, and that Allen was not at his best but the team won anyway.

injuries.detail: Left the game; Brady said he had no report yet and would evaluate after the game.

signals.claim: Cook remains the featured back and will keep getting the ball despite fumble issues.
signals.note: Cook has had a ball punched out in two straight games but Brady is publicly backing his workload, which is positive for his volume.
signals.quote: that's not going to stop me from giving you the ball the next play

signals.claim: Ty Johnson will keep a meaningful offensive role after making big plays in this game.
signals.note: Johnson made a fourth-down play and a big third-down conversion, which could increase his role in the offense.
signals.quote: Ty's on the field. Good things usually happen.

signals.note: Brady praised Gore's first two weeks and was glad to get him back, which suggests a share of the backfield work but no clear change in role.
signals.quote: Frank obviously did an outstanding job the first two weeks

signals.claim: Kincaid needs to secure the ball better after his fumble while fighting for yards.
signals.note: The fumble in a close game was a ball-security concern, but Brady framed it as coachable rather than a role issue.

signals.claim: Rousseau will keep rushing from a two-point stance with better vision, and his sack production can continue.
signals.note: Back-to-back two-sack games and a role change point to continued pass-rush production for IDP managers.
signals.quote: he's playing a little different position. He has eyes in the backfield.

signals.claim: Gardner-Johnson is back on the field and in the defensive rotation after a week of practice.
signals.note: His interception was a game-changing play, and a full practice week should help his IDP outlook.
signals.quote: So proud of CD man. Just finally getting out there.

signals.claim: Igbinosun will get extra snaps while Benford is out.
signals.note: He played more after Benford's injury and Brady praised his confidence, so he could carry IDP value if Benford misses time.
signals.quote: that guy definitely doesn't blink, right?

signals.claim: Hairston is expected to keep working in the cornerback rotation while Benford is out.
signals.note: Brady mentioned that Hairston will want a first-drive play back, which suggests he made a mistake but is still in the mix.
signals.quote: Max is going to want that first drive back

signals.claim: Benford's injury will be evaluated after the game.
signals.note: He left the game and Brady had no update, which affects the secondary depth chart.
signals.quote: Nothing yet.

signals.claim: Brady will review the protection issues that led to hits on Allen.
signals.note: Allen was not at his best and took pressure, but Brady said the team will keep riding with him.
signals.quote: we're always going to ride along with Josh

topics.detail: Five turnovers drew heavy blame from Brady, who said he has been talking about "smoke detectors" and needs to coach technique and call a better game.
Brady said breakdowns that led to hits on Josh Allen could come from play calling, protection, technique or routes, and that he would study the tape starting with his own play calling.
Brady told the team at halftime the situation was "perfect" to see how they would respond, and was proud that nobody pointed fingers.
Brady said he is still learning the stadium and conditions, nothing notable yet, and the crowd was loud and helped cause penalties on third downs.

title: Dave Canales evaluates Week 3 game vs. Browns
headline: Panthers' run game still unproductive; Coker (quad) and Michael Jackson (groin) both left injured, Bryce Young played through a lower-body issue, and Waller's red zone snaps are 'something we can look at'.
summary: Canales called the loss a game of execution, citing red zone drives that ended in field goals, missed early turnover chances, untimely penalties, and a costly roughing-the-passer call that extended Cleveland's final drive. He credited the Browns for a disciplined plan and said the run game, which he says has not been efficient from the start of games this season, was hurt by missed blocks against a quick front. Bryce Young was pressured often and was in the medical tent; Canales confirmed a lower-body issue, said he was cleared and finished, and suggested it may have affected a few throws. Jalen Coker left with a quad problem and Michael Jackson with a groin injury, and a lineman (apparently Jake Curhan) hurt his quad on the last touchdown play; all will be evaluated this week. Canales said the Browns covered Tremayne and Waller closely with a mix of man and zone, and that coaches need to put them in better positions. He said John Metchie III and David Moore stepped in, with Moore coming open over the middle on the last drive. On Waller's absence from some red zone snaps, he cited play-call mix and tendencies, and said Waller has a package role that can be revisited. He defended going for it on fourth-and-1 twice, saying the decisions were right but the execution wasn't there.

injuries.detail: Quad tightened up and the pain wasn't going away. Strength was tested, but he couldn't return. Canales gave no timeline.
Groin injury after chasing across the field and hitting the ground. He was nowhere near returning, and the extent is not yet known.
Worked through a lower-body issue, went to the medical tent, was cleared and finished the game. More information to come after a full evaluation.
Appears to be the 'Jake' who hurt a quad on the final touchdown play. He did not return and will be evaluated.

signals.claim: Coker's quad injury could affect his availability this week; he will be evaluated.
signals.note: WR depth is thin if Coker misses time, which raises the roles of Metchie and Moore.
signals.quote: his quad lit up on him a little bit

signals.claim: Jackson's groin injury will be evaluated this week and the extent is unknown.
signals.note: A groin injury where he couldn't put weight on the leg puts his availability in doubt.
signals.quote: he was nowhere close to getting back out there during this this game

signals.claim: Young is working through a lower-body injury that may have affected his throws.
signals.note: Monitor his practice status; a lower-body issue could limit his accuracy and mobility.
signals.quote: he's working through something. But he was able to finish.

signals.claim: Metchie is a receiver who can step in when others are out.
signals.note: With Coker and Jackson hurt, he is in line for a bigger role.
signals.quote: I'm glad we have guys like John Metchie

signals.claim: Moore can step in for injured receivers; he was coming open over the middle on the last drive.
signals.note: A possible increase in targets if the WR injuries linger.
signals.quote: David Moore, um, who was really coming open right at the end

signals.claim: Waller's red zone and package usage may be revisited after he sat out some red zone snaps.
signals.note: His TD upside depends on red zone snaps, and Canales left the door open to a change.
signals.quote: Darren has has his role in his package as well.

signals.claim: Coaches will look at getting Tremayne better positioned after he was covered closely and targeted once in the second half.
signals.note: A quiet game, but Canales wants him to be a big part of the offense.
signals.quote: We want him to be a big part of our of what we're doing.

topics.detail: The offensive line missed blocks against a quick Browns front. Canales says the run game is not yet efficient from the start of games this season, though it became the feature of the late touchdown drive.
Canales said there was nothing too exotic from Cleveland, other than possibly being late on one slot pressure. Pressure forced Young to get the ball out earlier than he wanted.
Carolina went for it on fourth-and-1 from its own 40 and on another attempt, and Canales called it an 'absolute no brainer.' He said the team will keep taking fourth downs that make sense.
A late-hit call on the pass rush extended Cleveland's final drive, and Canales said the defense must contain Deshaun Watson better and rush with discipline.

title: Zac Taylor Meets With Media Following Week 3 | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Bengals fall 30-27 to Pittsburgh. Zac Taylor gave no player-specific fantasy news, but safeties Kyle Dugger and Bryan Cook both left banged up.
summary: Taylor said all three phases had a chance to win in the fourth quarter and none made the play. He credited Pittsburgh with making more plays and said the Bengals did not earn the win. He called the final drive good until the fumble, with Cincinnati around the 38 and playing to score rather than kick a field goal. He said the defense needed a stop after two big explosive plays on Pittsburgh's last scoring drive, one of which included a holding call. He pointed to special teams as a swing factor: a roughing-the-kicker penalty led to a Pittsburgh touchdown and a muffed punt led to a field goal, ten points in all. The defense allowed 411 yards after a strong start to the season, and Taylor declined to pinpoint why before watching the tape. He said Pittsburgh's quarterback hit early RPOs, got the ball out quickly and bought time when needed. Asked about the safeties, he said Dugger and Cook were both banged up, with no further detail.

injuries.detail: Taylor confirmed he was banged up in the game but gave no diagnosis or timeline.
Appears to be the 'Brian' who came in late; Taylor said both safeties were banged up, with no diagnosis or timeline.

signals.note: Dugger got banged up in the game, so check his practice participation this week, especially in IDP leagues.
signals.quote: Both of them were banged up.

signals.note: Cook also got banged up late, so his availability is worth tracking in IDP leagues.

topics.detail: Taylor said the offense, defense and special teams each had a chance to win in the fourth quarter. The offense was driving near the 38 when the fumble ended its last drive, and the defense couldn't get a stop on the final Pittsburgh drive.
Taylor said special teams cost ten points: a roughing-the-kicker penalty extended a drive that ended in a Pittsburgh touchdown, and a muffed punt led to a field goal.

The defense allowed 411 yards after a strong start to the season. Taylor said he would study the tape before explaining the drop-off, and credited Pittsburgh's quick RPO throws and the quarterback buying time.
Taylor said the team is 2-1 and wanted to be 3-0. He said next week will show what the team is made of, with the next game at home.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference | Week 3 vs. Carolina Panthers
headline: Browns beat Carolina 21-18 to move to 2-1; Monken says the run game improved but the passing offense is still not right, Harold Fannin Jr. is coming on, and Pittsburgh visits Thursday night for first place in the division.
summary: Monken praised the team's resiliency after the 21-18 win and gave most of the credit to a defense that held Carolina to field goals after turnovers and got the final stop. He was blunt that the offense has not been good enough in coaching or play, citing penalties, a fumble, and three straight non-scoring drives to start the second half. Deshaun Watson struggled for stretches but scored on a scramble touchdown, got knocked down and came back into the game, and made the key plays at the end including the two-point conversion. Monken called Watson's legs one of his superpowers, and said the passing game still needs work as Watson learns the system and cleans up his eyes and drops. The run game was better and more downhill, especially before halftime, but it still has a long way to go. Harold Fannin Jr. had a great game and Monken said the sky is the limit for him, while Denzel Boston was targeted late because Monken, the play caller, had not thrown to him enough. Mekhi Blackmon filled in for Tyson Campbell, got tested early, and settled in, and Monken also praised Mason Graham's growth toward consistency. The team turns to a short week against Pittsburgh on Thursday night with first place in the division at stake.

injuries.detail: Was knocked down on the scramble touchdown play and had to leave briefly, but signaled he was good and returned to the game, finishing with the two-point conversion.
Mekhi Blackmon played in his place early in the game; no reason or injury detail was given.

signals.claim: Watson will keep making plays with his legs while the passing game still needs to improve.
signals.note: His rushing production gives him a fantasy floor, but Monken admitted the passing offense is inconsistent and said he 'probably didn't play as well as he wanted.'
signals.quote: that's one of his superpowers as he continues to learn the system

signals.claim: The game plan had more opportunities for Fannin that were not reached, and he is expected to keep growing as a featured matchup piece.
signals.note: Monken praised him strongly and said more targets were planned, which is a good sign for his TE fantasy outlook.
signals.quote: the sky's the limit with him because he he'll work to be physical.

signals.claim: Boston should get more targets when the offense is in rhythm, and Monken blamed himself for not throwing to him enough.
signals.note: Monken said the lack of flow, not Boston, limited his production; he caught a bunch of balls when the offense was in rhythm last week.
signals.quote: I got to throw it to him

signals.claim: Blackmon filled in for Tyson Campbell and played more comfortably as the game went on.
signals.note: Matters for IDP and matchup depth if Campbell's absence continues, though Campbell's status is unclear.
signals.quote: to go out there and battle and, uh, you know, a real credit to him.

signals.claim: Graham is growing toward more consistent play rather than just flashes.
signals.note: Positive for IDP interior defensive line value as he develops in year two.
signals.quote: we're going to be less flashy and more consistent, and I'm happy for him.

topics.detail: Monken said the run game was better and more downhill, especially in the late first-half drive that reached the red zone, but there is still plenty to clean up. He said the backs can hit it more downhill and that play-calling can improve.

Monken said the late fourth-and-one try was a 50/50 call after the offense botched second down. He thought a field goal would have forced Carolina to score a touchdown, but they went for it and the defense held.

Monken said the offense had no flow in the second half after a fumble and three straight possessions without points. He called out penalties, missed throws, and poor calls, and said the offense needs to get first downs and stack plays.

title: Campbell on Week 3 performance
headline: Lions beat the Jets to go 2-1. Gibbs took over in the second half, Goff played a smart game, and a backup back earned enough trust to take a little workload off Gibbs.
summary: Campbell called it a win that took all three phases. The Jets played hard and had a chance at the end, and Detroit's defense sealed it with a late stop on a call from Kevin Shepard. Chuck Clark forced a fumble and Jack Campbell recovered it. Campbell said the Thursday-night loss wasn't who the Lions are and that this was the response he wanted. He said Jahmyr Gibbs found another gear in the second half as the blocking improved, and that he loves Gibbs' downhill runs as much as the perimeter ones. Jared Goff got praise for patience and smart decisions, working through checkdowns and shots while carrying a heavy load of kills and checks. Campbell said getting everyone involved was a deliberate plan by the offensive play caller. He credited Isaac TeSlaa for winning deep and said the threat of that speed opens up the route tree. In the secondary, Roger McCreary got a look at outside corner but will still play nickel. Campbell said all the corners were available and he is willing to use any of them. He also said a backup running back gained trust with pass protection against Demario Davis's blitzes and some real runs, which lets the Lions lighten Gibbs' load.

signals.claim: Gibbs will keep being used on downhill runs as well as perimeter touches, though a backup back may take some snaps to keep him fresh.
signals.note: He was the engine of the late-game offense and made big plays as a runner, but Campbell hinted at managing his workload.
signals.quote: he hit another gear once we got him going there

signals.claim: Goff will keep carrying a heavy responsibility in the offense, with many kills and checks put on him each week.
signals.note: Campbell is very confident in Goff's decision-making, which supports steady QB production.
signals.quote: Just the guy playing at a high level at the quarterback position.

signals.claim: TeSlaa's speed will keep being used on deep outs and daggers, and defenses will have to account for him.
signals.note: He is emerging as a deep threat and could see more targets if he keeps winning downfield.
signals.quote: Tesla did a hell of a job.

signals.claim: McCreary will play some outside corner but still be used at nickel, with Rakestraw or Ya-Sin rotating in.
signals.note: A rotating corner room matters mainly for IDP value and for how Detroit defends the slot.
signals.quote: let's give Roger a shot down there outside and still use him though at nickel

signals.note: His forced fumble sealed the win, which helps his case for safety snaps and IDP value.
signals.quote: Chuck Clark comes up with a huge fumble

topics.topic: Defensive call to close the game
topics.detail: Campbell lauded Kevin Shepard's late-game call and said the defense had to win the game, which it did with the Clark fumble and a recovery by Jack Campbell.
Campbell said the play caller did a heck of a job and that getting everyone involved was a concerted effort. The Lions still lean on their core players when the game tightens.

McCreary got a look outside, and Rakestraw and Ya-Sin rotate depending on whether McCreary slides inside. Campbell said all corners were available and he would use them if needed. He praised Garrett Wilson's contested catches but accepted them as long as his defense stayed in phase.

topics.topic: Backup RB trust and pass protection
topics.detail: Against Demario Davis's blitzing, an unnamed backup back stepped up in pass protection, allowing for some big, unflashy runs. Campbell said growing trust there lets the Lions take a little off Gibbs.
Campbell said last Thursday night wasn't indicative of the team, and that this game showed the Lions playing sound, aggressive football with urgency.

title: DeMeco Ryans on Texans at Colts, Three Takeaways & Moving Forward
headline: Texans fall to 0-3 after loss at Indianapolis; Ryans takes blame, Nico Collins is progressing and could return soon, and Mario Edwards has a knee injury that needs further testing.
summary: Ryans opened by saying the team is 0-3, that it all starts with him, and that the result is not good enough even though he liked the week of preparation. He was pressed on clock management late in the game (not calling a timeout with time left) and on the decision to go for it on fourth-and-one. He said he believed in the play call and wanted to finish the drive with a touchdown, and he used the Hail Mary at the end rather than kicking. He credited the defense for three takeaways and some good D-line play, but said the unit could not get off the field on third down, while the offense could not sustain drives or convert third downs. Asked about the offensive line's up-and-down play, he only said the staff will dive into the film and look for improvements. He did not rule out changes, saying they will take 24 hours, reset, and evaluate from there. On injuries, Mario Edwards is being evaluated for a knee injury and the extent is unknown. He praised the receivers (Jared Wayne, Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte) for making plays, and said Nico Collins has been progressing well and may return this week.

injuries.detail: Knee injury; extent unknown, further testing planned.
Has been progressing really well; the team will see how the week goes to decide if he can get back out there.

signals.claim: Collins may return to the field this week depending on how practice goes.
signals.note: A Collins return would restore Houston's top receiver and boost the value of the entire passing game.
signals.quote: Niko's been progressing really well. So we'll see how this week goes

signals.note: Made a big catch in the second half and is part of a spread-the-ball receiving group while Collins is out.
signals.quote: J. Wayne caught a big one there.

signals.note: Made an outstanding catch to put the offense in striking distance, which could help his role.
signals.quote: an outstanding catch by Hutch there

signals.note: Cited among the receivers making plays; target share may stay fluid until Collins returns.
Ryans cited him as making a nice play, and he is part of a rotating target group.
signals.quote: KB made a nice play as well.

signals.claim: Edwards will undergo further testing on his knee to determine the severity.
signals.note: A knee injury of unknown extent could remove a depth piece from the Houston defense.
signals.quote: We're still evaluating Mario for the knee.

topics.detail: Ryans took responsibility for not calling a timeout late, and defended going for it on fourth-and-one because he believed in the play and players. He said the Hail Mary was chosen over a kick at the end.
The defense forced three turnovers and the D-line played well at times, but the unit couldn't get off the field on third down.
The offense struggled to sustain drives and convert third downs, with two good second-half drives. Ryans gave no specifics on the offensive line, only that the staff will review film.
At 0-3, Ryans stressed unity ('a divided house cannot stand') and left open the possibility of changes after a 24-hour reset.

title: Shane Steichen: Colts vs. Texans postgame
headline: Colts survive Texans 19-17; Josh Downs and Keenan Allen produced explosive plays, Tyler Warren got volume without yards, and kicker Spencer Shrader played through a groin tweak.
summary: Steichen praised the defense for holding Houston to 223 total yards, forcing five three-and-outs and stopping the run. Kicker Spencer Shrader tweaked his groin in warmups about 15 minutes before the game, but he still played, with Rigo handling kickoffs. Shrader then hit a 58-yarder and a 53-yarder, and kicked the game-winning field goal with about 20 seconds left. Steichen said Daniel Jones played well and was efficient, but he put the ball on the ground in the pocket against a heavy pass rush, leading to three turnovers. He singled out Josh Downs for explosive plays, a big third-down catch on a sail route, and option routes, and credited the Downs-Jones rapport. Keenan Allen and Laquan Treadwell made deep end-breaker plays, and Allen caught a slant on the final drive. Tyler Warren had plenty of catches on underneath and over-the-middle routes, but few yards against a defense that limits explosive plays. The win moves Indy to 1-2 in the division race, and the team now prepares to travel to London.

injuries.detail: Tweaked his groin in warmups about 15 minutes before the game, but played, and made kicks of 58 and 53 yards plus the game-winner. Rigo handled kickoffs.
Praised for his comeback from a significant injury. He had a sack in the game and is playing at his usual level.

signals.claim: Will remain a featured target for Daniel Jones on end-breakers, option routes, and third downs.
signals.note: Steichen highlighted Downs' repeated explosive plays and chemistry with Jones, which points to a steady slot role.
signals.quote: He keeps showing up. Hit him on an end breaker.

signals.claim: Warren will keep getting underneath and over-the-middle targets while the offense works to develop his role.
signals.note: His volume is solid, but yardage is limited when the opponent takes away explosive plays.
signals.quote: Obviously the yards weren't there, but you know, that's a defense

signals.claim: Allen is a trusted option on key downs, including the slant on third down in the final drive, and on deep end-breaker plays.
signals.note: He is a reliable target in crucial situations and also hit deep shots.

signals.claim: Treadwell will be a deep-shot option when the coverage and protection look is right.
signals.note: He had an end-breaker catch and a big play on the last drive, so he may have some deep-threat value.
signals.quote: hitting the big ball there and there to tread there at the end was huge.

signals.claim: Jones needs to secure the ball better in the pocket after three turnovers.
signals.note: He was efficient and led the winning drive, but ball security is a risk against pass-rush-heavy defenses.
signals.quote: He just got a hold on the ball.

topics.detail: The defense limited Houston to 223 yards, had five three-and-outs, and stopped the run. Steichen credited good communication, tackling, and gap discipline.

Shrader's groin tweak limited him in the pregame process. Steichen said he is comfortable with Shrader's range as long as the ball is around the 40 to 48-yard line. The late conservative play-calling was meant to get Shrader into range.
Steichen called the win big because it was a division game, and said every team in the division may be 1-2. Next is a trip to London.

title: Andy Reid: 'We Knew It [Would] Be Four Quarters of Football, And That's What It Took' | Postgame Press Conference - NFL Week 3
headline: Reid reported no injuries after the Chiefs moved to 3-0 with a hard-fought win over Miami, and he named no individual players.
summary: Andy Reid opened by saying he had no injuries to report so far after the win over the Dolphins. He praised Miami for playing hard for four quarters, noting they are a young team like the Chiefs and fly around the field. He said the Chiefs have plenty to work on but also took some good things from the game, and he is happy to be 3-0. Reid pointed to the second half, when the defense got some stops and the offense capitalized on a couple of them. He called special teams solid. In response to a question about the Dolphins, he said their players play hard on every snap, which shows they are listening to and trusting their head coach. He called that coach a sharp guy with a good staff who can build on it. He did not discuss any individual players, roles or usage.

topics.detail: Reid said there were no injuries to report so far after the game, which is a clean bill of health for fantasy purposes, though it was an early assessment.

Reid said the game took four quarters. The defense produced stops in the second half and the offense converted a couple of them into points. Special teams were solid, and he said there are still things to clean up.
Reid praised Miami as a young, hard-playing team that plays hard every snap. He credited their head coach and staff for the buy-in.

title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Bills
headline: Harbaugh offered no player-specific fantasy info after a Week 3 loss to Buffalo; the Chargers' offense is not scoring despite five defensive takeaways, and he ruled out significant offensive changes.
summary: Harbaugh was terse and non-specific after the loss, repeatedly saying the team 'hasn't been good enough yet' and refusing to single out any player, positively or negatively. He noted the defense forced five turnovers and the offense created opportunities and moved the ball (first downs), but it failed to finish drives with touchdowns and left points on the field. He specifically pointed to a drive from the team's own 10-yard line that stalled near the goal line, with a costly penalty pushing the offense back at second-and-goal. He said there is no thought of significant offensive changes and that he believes in the players and coaches. He cited the team's fight and competitiveness as reasons for hope and framed the fix as 'chipping away.' Asked about injuries and a possible new player entering the mix, he declined to evaluate individuals before watching the tape. On whether there is a disconnect between scheme and execution, he conceded that coaches always wish they'd called a different play but gave no concrete diagnosis, and he said he couldn't say for sure whether the issues stem from mental lapses or from still getting comfortable with the offense.

topics.detail: Harbaugh said the offense generated first downs and opportunities, helped by five defensive takeaways, but did not finish drives in the end zone. He said the team left points out there, including a stalled drive near the goal line.

He ruled out significant offensive changes, saying he believes in the players and coaches. He did not diagnose whether the problems are mental lapses or a lack of comfort with the offense, saying 'I really can't say for sure.'
A penalty after the offense reached second-and-goal near the goal line was costly. He called penalties a recurring problem and said the team hasn't been good enough in critical moments.
The team is 0-3 by his own account of the first two weeks and this game. He said he is focused only on the current game, and he takes hope from the team's fight and competitiveness.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 9/27: "We have to fix a lot of things"
headline: Vrabel is openly concerned about Drake Maye's turnovers and hesitation after a Week 3 loss to Jacksonville, but he insists Maye knows what to do. Caleb Lomu got late-game reps in place of Morgan Moses, and Vrabel says Moses' job isn't in jeopardy.
summary: Vrabel opened by saying his concern level for the team is very high, and he pointed to turnovers, penalties, missed red-zone chances, missed kicks and poor sudden-change play as the reasons for the loss. He took blame for the problems but kept coming back to Drake Maye's decision-making with the ball, saying 'we haven't made good decisions' and that Maye can't force plays. He defended Maye as a 24-year-old who knows the formations and plays but needs to be more confident reacting to defenses and knowing when to hit the first read or check down. He also said the players around Maye must do their jobs, including protecting him from pressure. He said the turnovers haven't shown up in practice at this rate, but that practice consistency needs to improve across all three phases. On the offensive line, Vrabel said Morgan Moses came out early because it was his own decision: he didn't think the team would come back, Moses is 36, and he wanted Caleb Lomu to get reps. He said Moses' starting job isn't in jeopardy as far as he's aware. Vrabel blamed the many pre-snap penalties on players jumping at Jacksonville's cadence. He said the run defense wore down after failing to get off the field on third down and missing a lot of tackles. He said the team is mostly focused on getting healthy and improving, with a road game at Buffalo next.

signals.claim: Maye will work through his turnover and hesitation issues; Vrabel says he knows what to do and needs to play more confidently and decisively.
signals.note: Maye has been turnover-prone and hesitant through three games, and a tough road matchup at Buffalo is next, so his fantasy floor is shaky.
signals.quote: We haven't made good decisions with the football.

signals.claim: Moses' starting job is not in jeopardy; he was pulled late as Vrabel's own decision in a game he thought was lost.
signals.note: Offensive line stability matters for Maye's protection, and Lomu is the next man up if Moses is truly pushed.
signals.quote: Not that I'm aware of.

signals.claim: Lomu got late-game reps in place of Moses, but he has not been named a starter.
signals.note: Lomu is a possible future starter at tackle, which could affect pass protection for Maye.
signals.quote: let's get Caleb some, some reps.

topics.detail: Vrabel blamed turnovers, missed red-zone chances, missed kicks, sudden-change lapses and pre-snap penalties for the loss, and said they must be fixed quickly.
Vrabel said the defense got tired after not getting off the field on third down, missed a ton of tackles and was worn down by Jacksonville's run game.
He said practice consistency in all three phases has to improve, and that turnovers like today's have not been showing up in practice.

title: Postgame Press Conference: Coach John Harbaugh on win over Titans
headline: Jameis Winston is the expected Week 4 starter at QB, though Harbaugh was lukewarm about his play. Brian Burns gets an MRI after leaving hurt, and Arvell Reese broke out with 14 tackles.
summary: Harbaugh praised the Giants for grinding out a low-scoring, ugly win over the Titans in tough conditions. He called it a field-position, turnover and run-game affair. The defense held up late and closed the game with Jevon Holland's interception after Tennessee reached the red zone. Harbaugh was unhappy with the offense's red-zone penalties and a botched first-and-goal wildcat call, but he praised the rookie kicker and the punt team. The run game finished with 138 yards against a strong Titans front. Harbaugh credited the offensive line, the receivers' blocking, and the backs. He gave Arvell Reese a game ball after a 14-tackle performance. On quarterback, he said Jameis Winston 'did what was required,' that the performance won't change the team's plans, and that he expects Winston to start next week. On injuries, Brian Burns will get an MRI with some hope for a good result. Patrick Ricard suffered a deep nose laceration.

injuries.detail: Left the game hurt. MRI expected Saturday night. Harbaugh said there is 'some hope' but nothing is known until the scan.
Suffered a deep nose laceration, possibly from a hand in his face mask. No word on availability.

signals.claim: Winston will be the Giants' starting QB in Week 4.
signals.note: He keeps the starting job for now, but Harbaugh's praise was minimal and he left room for roster moves at QB.
signals.quote: I thought he did what was required. He did what was necessary.

signals.note: Reese had 14 tackles and a game ball, which makes him a strong IDP option.
signals.quote: He was definitely all over the field today.

signals.note: Holland made the game-winning interception and has been the defense's turnover producer through three games, which helps IDP value.
signals.quote: That's the kind of player Javon Holland has always been

signals.claim: Burns will have an MRI on Saturday night; his status depends on the result.
signals.note: Burns is a key pass rusher, so his MRI result matters for IDP managers.
signals.quote: Brian Burns will get an MRI hopefully tonight.

signals.note: Skattebo handled a tough workload in the run game, and the offense also called a wildcat direct snap to him near the goal line.
signals.quote: had a lot of tough yards against against a tough run defense

signals.note: Harris was part of an effective committee in a 138-yard rushing day, so his role looks steady.

topics.detail: Harbaugh was unhappy with penalties that pushed the offense out of scoring position inside the ten. He called it a major point of emphasis. He also said the first-and-goal wildcat play did not involve a throw and was 'not our finest moment.'
He praised the rookie kicker for making field goals in poor conditions. He also credited the punt team for long punts and coverage that flipped field position.

The defense held Tennessee to about one first down in the first half and stayed composed in the late red-zone stand. Harbaugh was pleased with the pressure but wants more sacks, and he was annoyed by offside penalties.
Harbaugh said Winston's performance will not influence the team's quarterback plans and that the team will use whatever options it has. He still expects Winston to start next week.

title: HC Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (9/27) | Week 3
headline: Kenyon Sadiq is getting every rep possible and the Jets want to feed him the ball. Geno Smith leaned on the tight ends after a key offensive player went down. Dylan Parham has a knee issue, and Garrett Wilson cleared a head evaluation.
summary: Aaron Glenn opened by saying Dylan Parham has a knee injury and that Garrett Wilson cleared a head evaluation and is fine. He promised updates on two other players he didn't clearly identify. He thought the defense was strong in the first half but let the opponent build momentum in the second half, and he took blame for not giving them better calls. Detroit's weapons (Gibbs, Jameson Williams, St. Brown and the receiver who got open on the long play) were hard to contain. Offensively, the first half was poor, but the unit found momentum after halftime. Glenn praised Geno Smith, saying he adjusted to heavy interior blitzing and well-set edges by getting the ball to his tight ends after a top player went down. He said Kenyon Sadiq is getting every rep possible, can play multiple positions, is athletically special and very smart, and the team wants to get him the ball. Glenn criticized missed scoring chances, including red-zone and two-minute drives, and kept returning to the idea of closing a small gap. The Jets lost a close game in which the defense allowed 31 points.

injuries.detail: Suffered a knee injury in the game. Glenn gave no further detail and said an update would come later.
Went through a head evaluation during the game and was cleared. Glenn said he is fine.

signals.claim: Sadiq will keep playing multiple tight end roles and the Jets will keep trying to get him the ball.
signals.note: Glenn said it is time to give him more to do, and a growing target share at TE is a stash and add signal.
signals.quote: he's getting every rep possible to be able to do that.

signals.claim: Smith will keep distributing the ball to tight ends and adjusting when the offense is disrupted or a key player is out.
signals.note: Glenn's praise suggests a stable QB situation with tight ends getting more targets.
signals.quote: I thought Geno did an outstanding job.

signals.claim: Wilson cleared his head evaluation and is not expected to be affected going forward.
signals.note: Glenn called him fine, so he looks safe to start barring a later setback.
signals.quote: Garrett's fine when it comes to this game.

signals.claim: Parham's knee injury will be updated later.
signals.note: A possible absence would affect the interior of the offensive line.
signals.quote: Parham has a knee.

topics.detail: Glenn liked the first half but said the second half slipped. He took responsibility for play calls and said the defense can't use the opponent's talent as an excuse after allowing 31 points.

The offense moved the ball poorly in the first half and missed chances at the end of the half. Glenn said they need to finish drives, including red-zone and two-minute situations, even if only for field goals.
Glenn repeatedly said the team is close and needs to close the gap, pointing to the team's competitive stamina and belief.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the win over the Bengals
headline: Jaylen Warren was the focal point of a 30-27 win, with Rico Dowdle's role shrinking as Warren takes most RB touches; both tight ends (Freiermuth, Washington) are primary targets; rookie Max Iheanachor and Brock Hoffman moved into the starting OL.
summary: McCarthy said the offense was much better in the 30-27 win over Cincinnati, crediting third-down production, an emphasis on big plays, and cleaner communication between the line, coaches and quarterbacks. He called Jaylen Warren 'huge' and the focal point, noting Warren had been limited in practice but came up big. He explained that early in the season Warren and Rico Dowdle were a one-two punch, but the team is now being more selective and letting Warren take as much work as he can handle, with Travis Homer and Lew Nichols III also in the mix. Max Iheanachor and Brock Hoffman entered the starting lineup at right tackle and right guard, a decision made earlier in the week after Iheanachor's training-camp injury setback. McCarthy said Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington are both primary targets and there was a conscious effort to get them the ball, though he wants more ball distribution across the whole perimeter. He praised Patrick Queen (13 tackles, a near interception) and the defensive close, including a big rush with a second fumble and play-calling from Patrick Graham that stayed calm. The team now turns quickly to a Thursday night game at Cleveland.

injuries.detail: McCarthy said Warren was limited in certain things in practice, but he played and was the focal point of the offense.
Had an injury setback in training camp; McCarthy said he is ready and was given the starting right tackle opportunity.

signals.claim: Warren will keep taking the majority of the RB touches, ahead of Rico Dowdle.
signals.note: Warren is now the lead back, with McCarthy saying the team is letting him take as much as he can, which raises his floor and ceiling.
signals.quote: just let Jalen take as much as he can.

signals.claim: Dowdle's share of the backfield work will be smaller than the early-season split.
signals.note: The early one-two punch has become more selective, which lowers Dowdle's touches.

signals.claim: Freiermuth will continue to be a primary target in the passing game.
signals.note: McCarthy called him a trusted focal point and said there was a conscious effort to get him the ball.
signals.quote: I would consider them both primary targets.

signals.claim: Washington will continue to be a primary target in the passing game.
signals.note: He and Freiermuth combined for close to 100 yards, and the plan is to keep involving the tight ends.
signals.quote: there was a conscious effort, conscious effort to try to get them the ball.

signals.claim: Iheanachor is now the starting right tackle.
signals.note: A better line helps the run game and Rodgers' pass protection, which supports the Pittsburgh offense overall.
signals.quote: Max is talented young man. I think that's evident.

signals.claim: Hoffman is now the starting right guard.
signals.note: He earned the starting spot after pushing for an opportunity and playing multiple interior spots.
signals.quote: he's been pushing, you know, pushing for an opportunity.

signals.claim: Queen will remain a key defensive playmaker.
signals.note: He led the team with 13 tackles, a tackle for loss and a pass defense, which makes him a strong IDP option.
signals.quote: I thought Patrick played very well.

signals.claim: Rodgers will keep distributing the ball more widely among the perimeter players.
signals.note: Ball distribution is a stated focus, which may spread targets among the perimeter players.
signals.quote: I thought Aaron was patient, uh, ball distribution.

topics.detail: McCarthy credited a heavier emphasis on third down, more volume in the specifics with fewer personnel groups, and better in-game communication between the line, coaches and quarterbacks. He noted they are not yet where they want to be on the passing game or distribution.
He praised Patrick Graham for not panicking as a play caller and keeping the calls clean in the four-minute defense. He also highlighted a big rush that produced a second fumble.
The team heads to Cleveland on a short week for a Thursday night game and will review the film tonight.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald: "We're Going To Go Back To Work And Get Better"
headline: Macdonald backed Sam Darnold and Jadarian Price despite turnovers in the loss at Washington, and said AJ Finley filled in well for Julian Love. The run game fizzled, and Macdonald said he would look at ways to run the ball better.
summary: Macdonald said Seattle lost a two-point game because of a minus-three turnover margin and poor situational football, and he credited Washington's plan and execution. He called Sam Darnold's day a microcosm of the game: the passing offense did good things and Darnold made tremendous on-time and extended plays, but the takeaways were costly. The run game never got going. Macdonald thought Washington had a good front, said Seattle searched for solutions, and said it leaned on the pass game in the second half as the weather cleared. He said the defense did not generate enough pressure to force takeaways, and that Seattle needs to be more aggressive. He called the red-zone play on both sides not good enough, especially in sudden-change situations on defense. He defended Jadarian Price after his fumbles, saying Price didn't return after the first one but was brought back after halftime and will be fine. He praised AJ Finley for stepping in on short notice with Julian Love out and said the secondary was organized, though some plays were missed. He closed by saying the team will go back to work, attack the problems, and "go through, not around."

injuries.detail: Was not playing in this game, forcing AJ Finley into the lineup on short notice. No specifics or timeline were given.
Did not return after his initial fumble, but Macdonald framed it as a ball-security issue and brought him back after halftime.

signals.claim: Darnold remains the starting QB and Macdonald is confident in his play despite the turnovers.
signals.note: Macdonald praised Darnold's playmaking and said he kept Seattle in the game, so the turnovers don't appear to threaten his job.
signals.quote: he kept us in the game.

signals.claim: Price will keep his role in the backfield despite the fumbles.
signals.note: The fumbles are a risk to his touches, but Macdonald publicly backed him, which suggests no immediate demotion.
signals.quote: He's going to figure it out. He'll be fine.

signals.claim: Finley filled in for Julian Love at safety and the secondary was organized with him in the lineup.
signals.note: Finley played well on short notice, so he could keep a bigger defensive role if Love is out again, which matters for IDP.
signals.quote: On a short couple of days notice. I thought he did a great job.

signals.claim: Love was unavailable for this game.
signals.note: His availability going forward will determine how much Finley plays, which matters for IDP.

topics.detail: Seattle was minus-three in takeaways and fell short in situational football and complementary football. Macdonald said the team needs to be more aggressive to create takeaways and apply pressure consistently.

The run game was ineffective against a good Washington front. Macdonald said Seattle shifted to the pass game in the second half as the weather cleared, and he named staying ahead of the sticks and running the ball better as areas to improve.
Macdonald said Seattle did not get enough pressure on the quarterback and did not hit its mark, and that Washington's pass protection was good.
Macdonald said red-zone play on both sides of the ball was not good enough, especially in sudden-change situations on defense, and said the staff will review its process.

On the late third-and-nine, he said Washington audibled against zero pressure and made a good check, and Seattle did not make the play. He said Seattle did not expect Washington to snap the ball before the two-minute warning but wanted to save the timeout.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Titans fall to 0-3 after a sluggish first half and a red-zone interception by Cam Ward; Saleh says Ward is not being benched.
summary: Saleh spoke after the Week 3 loss to the Giants, which dropped Tennessee to 0-3. He said the offense played well in the second half but started too slowly, citing drops and missed chances to move the ball. The offense reached the red zone three times and failed to score on two of those trips. One of those ended in a Cam Ward interception on first-and-goal from the 8 with two timeouts left, which Saleh said was unnecessary because the team was going to score anyway. He told Ward to keep his head up, and he flatly rejected the idea of sitting Ward down. On defense, the Giants had an eight-minute drive, but Tennessee held them to a field goal after a goal-line stand. The team also had a wasted timeout from an equipment problem with the Mike linebacker, which Saleh took responsibility for. He called kickoff mistakes a point of emphasis after a kicker lost two kickoffs, and defended the decision to try a 59-yard field goal that missed. He ended by promising to review the tape and have better answers the next day. He also gave only vague injury information: one player has an ankle issue, and another player came out briefly but finished the game.

injuries.detail: Saleh said the player is dealing with an ankle and that the team will run tests. The transcript does not make clear who it is.
Left the game and reported something, but returned and finished the game. Nothing further was given, and the name is too unclear to match to the roster.

signals.claim: Ward remains the starting quarterback and will not be benched despite the red-zone interception.
signals.note: Ward's job looks safe, but the red-zone interception and slow offensive starts keep his weekly fantasy outlook shaky.
signals.quote: Just be smarter with the football.

topics.detail: Asked about the first-half struggles, Saleh admitted the offense 'wasn't good enough' and pointed to drops and missed chances to move the ball. He said he would look at the tape, including the play calling, and have better answers the next day.
The offense got into the red zone three times in the second half and failed to score on two of them. One ended with Ward's interception on first-and-goal from the 8 with two timeouts left.

Saleh defended attempting a 59-yard field goal because points are at a premium. He said the kicker had the distance and simply missed it. He called the two lost kickoffs a point of emphasis that has to be fixed.
The Giants had a long drive in the third quarter of about eight minutes. Saleh credited them for mixing run and pass, and said the defense's goal-line stand held them to a field goal.

Saleh took the blame for a timeout taken after the Giants' timeout, caused by an equipment issue with the Mike linebacker's helmet. He said the officials missed a forward-progress call on a Titans tackle. He also explained that a ball carrier pushed backwards in a two-minute situation keeps the clock running.
At 0-3, Saleh said the message is unchanged: prepare with elite process and play with elite effort and strain. He said the team will eventually learn to win these close games.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 09/27/26
headline: Washington beat the defending champs 1-2 with Marcus Mariota at QB, Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs and Rachaad White all contributing; Leo Chenal is in the hospital, Percy Butler is in the concussion protocol, and Jayden Daniels' London status is still open.
summary: Quinn opened with injury news: LB Leo Chenal is in the hospital with feeling in his extremities and undergoing further testing, and S Percy Butler is in the concussion protocol. Washington got its first win after two losses, helped by takeaways: Kain Medrano stepped into Chenal's spot and intercepted a pass, and Sonny Styles forced a fumble and showed off his speed and length in coverage. Quinn gave game balls to Medrano and Mariota. Mariota ran the offense and closed the game by keeping the ball on a late third down, and Quinn said you put the ball in his and Jayden Daniels' hands at the end. He credited Rachaad White's run and Stefon Diggs' late first-down catch, said McLaurin had a big game and a good block, and noted Antonio Williams missed a play he'll want back. Quinn said the defense still has plenty to clean up, and the team had false starts and procedure penalties. He hopes to get some injured players back next week and the week after, and the team doesn't leave for London until Tuesday night. A big meeting Monday will decide who travels, since more players were banged up, and Daniels is still rehabbing.

injuries.detail: In the hospital. He has feeling in his extremities and is undergoing further testing tonight.
In the concussion protocol. Quinn will update once he knows more.
Still rehabbing an injury. Quinn said the London travel plan will be settled after Monday's meeting and he and the GM talk, with the team leaving Tuesday night.

signals.claim: Mariota keeps running the offense while Daniels is out and is trusted with the ball in late-game situations.
signals.note: Quinn praised Mariota and gave him a game ball. He remains the QB until Daniels is cleared, which supports the Washington passing game.
signals.quote: very little chance Marcus was given that one off

signals.claim: Whether Daniels travels to London will be decided after a Monday meeting, with the team leaving Tuesday night.
signals.note: Quinn gave no timeline and mostly talked about the plan with Mariota, so Daniels' availability for next week is unresolved.

signals.claim: White is a trusted contributor in key moments, with a big run and a clean late-game performance.
signals.note: Quinn singled him out for a big run and for answering the bell when the game was on the line, so he is a usable RB.
signals.quote: The run to Rashad I thought was a big one.

signals.claim: McLaurin remains the focal point of the passing game.
signals.note: Quinn praised his big game and said he also blocked well, so he is a secure WR1 with Mariota.
signals.quote: I was certainly pumped for Terry tonight too

signals.claim: Diggs is a reliable target on key downs.
signals.note: Quinn highlighted his late first-down catch with run after the catch as one of the biggest plays.
signals.quote: He's got great feel into that space where he had to get the first down.

signals.claim: Williams missed a play that Quinn thinks he will want back, but he keeps the coaches' confidence.
signals.note: A drop or missed chance was acknowledged, but Quinn showed no sign of reducing his role.
signals.quote: we've got like so much confidence in him.

signals.claim: Medrano steps into Chenal's role while Chenal is out.
signals.note: He intercepted a pass, earned a game ball, and could see more defensive snaps. That matters mostly for IDP.
signals.quote: he's got great hands.

signals.claim: Styles continues to play a big role as the defense's linebacker, without Luvu next to him, and is producing big plays.
signals.note: Quinn pointed to his interception, forced fumble and coverage on a man-to-man shot down the sideline, which is good for IDP.
signals.quote: he's capable of producing the ball based on the speed and length.

signals.claim: Chenal's availability is uncertain pending further testing.
signals.note: He was hospitalized, and Medrano filled his role.

signals.claim: Butler is in the concussion protocol, with an update to come.
signals.note: He could miss next week depending on how he clears the protocol.
signals.quote: Percy Butler, um, is in the concussion protocol.

topics.detail: Quinn said the defense produced takeaways to fill the wall in his office. He felt strong against the run and on early third downs. He said there is plenty to clean up and he will have a better assessment tomorrow.

Quinn said the team shifted players around at corner and on the offensive line to put its best groups on the field. Several players were banged up in this game, and he hopes to get some back next week and the week after.
Washington had false starts and procedure penalties that Quinn said it has to clean up, though the team overcame them.
The team flies out Tuesday night. A big meeting Monday will sort out who travels, including the status of Daniels, who is rehabbing.
Quinn praised Robertson as a true competitor with a lasting chip on his shoulder and called him an excellent addition and one of the team's leaders.
